name: zephyr-mqtt-stop

adapter_config.broker_name: Mosquitto 2.x -> Zephyr EviCon firmware (native_sim, stop mode)

system_version: Zephyr v4.2.0 EviCon firmware (native_sim/native/64, -evc_mode=stop) + eclipse-mosquitto:2.0.20 (evicon_review.py records the firmware SHA-256 and the Zephyr revision)

testbed.owner: VM-E zephyr-cutoff.exe -evc_mode=stop (native_sim/native/64, built by deploy/setup/build_iot.sh) + evicon-plant -tcp 127.0.0.1:18092

notes: Run with: python3 evicon_review.py measure zephyr-stop (release 074), after 'bash deploy/setup/build_iot.sh start' reports BUILD_OK. The cutoff mode plus the per-identity stop (durable tombstone table, EVC_TOMB_SLOTS entries; a full table answers UNCERTAIN TOMBSTONE_TABLE_FULL, never a silent drop). P9N measures the stop. Data and control paths as for zephyr-mqtt. Release 074 (experiment C2): one firmware binary, three evidence modes chosen at start (-evc_mode); the driver starts it with -evc_mode=cutoff|stop|plain, -evc_device=zephyr-1 and VM-B's broker on the command line. Commands are published with QoS 1 (at least once: the usual MQTT command channel, and the call shape of 068-070), the call shape experiment C2 uses. P9 (stop, then the held request arrives) measures Q_S; P9N its tombstone under pressure.
fault_model: network loss/delay, client abandon; owner up (no owner crash or reboot)
